Primary subject: the renovated Berlaymont building in Brussels, the European Commission headquarters, viewed from an elevated oblique aerial camera. Its defining geometry is ONE central circulation hub with EXACTLY FOUR long office wings of UNEQUAL lengths radiating outward as an asymmetric cross. Show each of the FOUR separate wing ends clearly, separated by open ground between wings. Keep the single central hub readable. The four wings are substantial multi-storey office slabs with gently curved facades, not straight abstract diagram arms. No additional wing, no closed courtyard and no separate tower.

Materials and architecture: pale silver-gray glass and steel facade, continuous floor glazing behind finely repeated movable glass sun-shading louvers on the VERTICAL facades. Flat roof planes with restrained plausible building services. Small, subdued light-orange terracotta cladding accents on a limited central frontage area; NOT a tall brown-red brick tower. The pale facade and four-wing form dominate the structure. The wings appear slightly elevated over a broad public esplanade due to the structural support arrangement. Architectural massing is a convincing approximation of the documented Berlaymont form, not a measured survey or technical plan.

Composition: own camera viewpoint, looking diagonally down at approximately 55 degrees, as from 250–300 m up; not directly top-down. Rotate the asymmetric cross diagonally in the frame so no rear wing is hidden behind the core. Include all four wings ENTIRELY with generous margins. The building is centered and occupies roughly 60 percent of the image width. Both roof shapes and multi-storey facade heights are apparent. A small portion of the Schuman street/square area appears in the foreground, with a subdued curved junction edge and a lightly planted public square; generic adjacent office buildings, streets and trees surround the building. The surroundings are illustrative urban context, not a claim of the exact October 2026 traffic plan. Keep the main four-wing silhouette legible at 480px.

Medium and lighting: realistic camera-shot architectural photograph appearance, muted natural colors, gentle diffuse daytime light with slight atmospheric haze. Buildings and streets reach the frame edges naturally; no artificial backdrop.
